common.footer_transactional: You are receiving this message because you have a {product} account. Transactional emails are part of the service and cannot be turned off.
common.footer_marketing: You are receiving this message because you agreed to hear from {product} about the product. It is not part of the service, and you can stop it whenever you like.
common.footer_unsubscribe_scope: That link stops product email only. The email the service needs to send you — failed-job alerts, security events, plan changes — keeps coming, because it is not marketing.
common.time_note: All times are shown in UTC.

welcome.subject: Welcome to {product}
welcome.preheader: Your account is ready. Here is how to get your first job running.
welcome.heading: Welcome to {product}
welcome.intro: Your account is ready. {product} runs the HTTP jobs you schedule, keeps the result of every run, and tells you when one of them stops working.
welcome.steps_heading: Three steps to your first job
welcome.step_1: Create a job: a schedule and the HTTP endpoint to call.
welcome.step_2: Pick the environment, staging or production, so a trial run never touches anything live.
welcome.step_3: Turn on failure alerts, so you hear about a broken job from us rather than from the people using your service.
welcome.docs: The documentation covers schedule expressions, retries and the cron.yaml file.

job_failed.subject: {job} is failing in {environment}
job_failed.preheader: A scheduled job has failed several times in a row.
job_failed.heading: A scheduled job is failing
job_failed.summary_one: {job} has failed {count} time in a row.
job_failed.summary_other: {job} has failed {count} times in a row.
job_failed.check_1: The endpoint is reachable and answers within the timeout the job allows.
job_failed.check_2: Any credentials the endpoint expects are still valid.
job_failed.check_3: The execution history holds the full response of every attempt.
job_failed.delivery_note: We cannot tell whether this message reached you, so please do not read the arrival of an alert as proof that the alerting works, nor its absence as proof that everything is fine. The execution history in the dashboard is the record to rely on.
job_failed.failure_timeout: The endpoint did not answer within the timeout.
job_failed.failure_connection: The connection to the endpoint could not be established.
job_failed.failure_dns: The host name of the endpoint could not be resolved.
job_failed.failure_tls: The TLS handshake with the endpoint failed.
job_failed.failure_unknown: The attempt failed for a reason the engine could not classify.

plan_changed.subject: Your {product} plan is now {next}
plan_changed.preheader: Your plan changed, and the limits that come with it are already in effect.
plan_changed.heading: Your plan changed
plan_changed.limits: How many jobs you can keep, how often they may run and how long their history is retained now follow the {next} plan.
plan_changed.suspended_heading: Some of your jobs are paused, and only you can choose what happens next
plan_changed.suspended_job_limit_one: {count} job is paused because the {next} plan allows fewer active jobs than you had running. We stopped all of them rather than pick for you — we cannot know which one matters most. Turn back on as many as the plan allows.
plan_changed.suspended_job_limit_other: {count} jobs are paused because the {next} plan allows fewer active jobs than you had running. We stopped all of them rather than pick for you — we cannot know which ones matter most. Turn back on as many as the plan allows.
plan_changed.suspended_resolution_one: {count} job is paused because it runs more often than the {next} plan permits. This one is not about room: change its schedule to an interval the plan allows, then turn it back on.
plan_changed.suspended_resolution_other: {count} jobs are paused because they run more often than the {next} plan permits. These are not about room: change their schedules to an interval the plan allows, then turn them back on.
plan_changed.suspended_nothing_lost: Nothing was deleted. Every paused job keeps its settings and its execution history, and stays exportable.
plan_changed.unexpected: If you were not expecting this change, write to {support}.

security_alert.subject: Security alert on your {product} account
security_alert.preheader: Something changed on your account that is worth a look.
security_alert.heading: Security alert
security_alert.kind_password_reset: The password of your account was reset.
security_alert.kind_api_key_created: A new API key was created on your account.
security_alert.kind_api_key_revoked: An API key of your account was revoked.
security_alert.kind_account_impersonated: An administrator opened your account to work on a support request. The access is recorded in the audit log.
security_alert.expected: If this was you, or someone on your team, there is nothing to do.
security_alert.unexpected: If it was not, change your password and revoke your API keys now, then write to {support}.
security_alert.phishing_note: {product} never asks you for your password or for an API key by email, and never sends either one in a message.

unsubscribe.title: Stop receiving product email
unsubscribe.question: Stop sending you email from {product} about the product?
unsubscribe.scope: This stops product email only. Failed-job alerts, security events and plan changes keep coming: they are how the service tells you things, and they are not marketing.
unsubscribe.done_body: No more product email will go out to this address. Nothing else about your account changes.
unsubscribe.already_body: This address is already set to receive no product email.
unsubscribe.resubscribe: Changed your mind? You can turn product email back on from your account settings.
unsubscribe.invalid_body: The address is incomplete or was altered along the way. Open the link from the message again, or write to {support} and we will take care of it.
